Linux
09/17/26
Stop trying to learn the entire Linux OS before applying for IT jobs.
From working with Linux in real environments, the basics matter far more at entry level:
• Navigate the filesystem
• Find/edit files
• Understand chmod & chown
• Install packages
• Read logs
• SSH into a server
You don't need a dual-boot setup either.
Windows? Use WSL.
Mac? Open Terminal.
The goal is simple: when someone says “SSH into the server and check what’s wrong,” you shouldn't freeze.

followups.text: Try a stale-search race: query "a" resolves after 800ms, "ab" after 100ms. Type a→ab quickly; the older result wrongly replaces the newer one. Fix with request IDs or cancellation. Verify: latest query wins, clearing the input stays empty, stale failures cannot set error, loading tracks only the active request. Use deterministic deferred promises in tests, then run the UI and inspect the diff in ADCode. No rush while travelling—share the failing/passing check when back.
